claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) in mammalian cells is driven by resilient machinery that includes >70 endocytic accessory proteins (EAP).
source: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) in mammalian cells is driven by resilient machinery that includes >70 endocytic accessory proteins (EAP).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about CME.

claim: Perturbation of individual EAPs often results in minor effects on biochemical measurements of CME.
source: Accordingly, perturbation of individual EAPs often results in minor effects on biochemical measurements of CME, thus providing inconclusive/misleading information regarding EAP function.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Unambiguously distinguishing abortive coats (ACs) from bona fide clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) is required but has been unaccomplished.
source: Live-cell imaging can detect earlier roles of EAPs preceding cargo internalization; however, this approach has been limited because unambiguously distinguishing abortive coats (ACs) from bona fide clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) is required but unaccomplished.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for developing DASC.

claim: DASC resolves ACs from CCPs based on single channel fluorescent movies.
source: Here, we develop a thermodynamics-inspired method, "disassembly asymmetry score classification (DASC)", that resolves ACs from CCPs based on single channel fluorescent movies.
evidence: This is the main methodological claim of the paper, stated in the abstract.

claim: DASC is a sensitive detector of phenotypic variation in CCP dynamics that is uncorrelated to the variation in biochemical measurements of CME.
source: We show that DASC is a sensitive detector of phenotypic variation in CCP dynamics that is uncorrelated to the variation in biochemical measurements of CME.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data comparing DASC measurements with transferrin uptake assays.

claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) is the major pathway for cellular uptake of macro-molecular cargo.
source: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) is the major pathway for cellular uptake of macro-molecular cargo (Kirchhausen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology, supported by citation.

claim: Clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) are specialized 100–200 nm wide patches at the plasma membrane created by a scaffold of assembled clathrin triskelia.
source: It is accomplished by concentrating cell surface receptors into specialized 100–200 nm wide patches at the plasma membrane created by a scaffold of assembled clathrin triskelia (Conner and Schmid, 2003).
evidence: This is a structural description of CCPs supported by citation.

claim: The initiation and stabilization of clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) is regulated by the AP2 (adaptor protein) complex.
source: The initiation and stabilization of these clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) is regulated by the AP2 (adaptor protein) complex (Cocucci et al., 2012), which recruits clathrin and binds to cargo and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) lipids.
evidence: This is supported by citation and is a well-established mechanism.

claim: The AP2 complex recruits clathrin and binds to cargo and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) lipids.
source: The initiation and stabilization of these clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) is regulated by the AP2 (adaptor protein) complex (Cocucci et al., 2012), which recruits clathrin and binds to cargo and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) lipids.
evidence: This describes the molecular function of AP2, supported by citation.

claim: Perturbing single EAPs like CALM or SNX9 often results in minor/uninterpretable changes in bulk biochemical measurements of cargo uptake.
source: Due to the resilience of CME, perturbing single EAPs, like CALM (Xiao et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2004), SNX9 (Posor et al., 2013; Bendris et al., 2016) etc., or even multiple EAPs (Aguet et al., 2013) often results in minor/uninterpretable changes in bulk biochemical measurements of cargo uptake.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations and is a key motivation for the study.

claim: Mutations in CALM are linked to Alzheimer's disease.
source: Nonetheless, perturbed EAP function can be physiologically consequential, e.g. mutations in CALM are linked to Alzheimer's disease (Harold et al., 2009) and SNX9 expression levels are correlated with cancer progression and other human diseases (Bendris and Schmid, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Harold et al., 2009.

claim: SNX9 expression levels are correlated with cancer progression and other human diseases.
source: Nonetheless, perturbed EAP function can be physiologically consequential, e.g. mutations in CALM are linked to Alzheimer's disease (Harold et al., 2009) and SNX9 expression levels are correlated with cancer progression and other human diseases (Bendris and Schmid, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bendris and Schmid, 2017.

claim: A large fraction of detected clathrin-coated structures (CSs) are shorter-lived (lifetimes < 20 seconds) than thought to be required for loading and internalizing cargo.
source: Using this imaging approach, we and others have observed that a large fraction of detected clathrin-coated structures (CSs) are shorter-lived (i.e. lifetimes < 20 seconds) than thought to be required for loading and internalizing cargo, and dimmer (i.e. exhibit lower intensities) than mature CCPs detected prior to internalization (Taylor et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This observation is supported by citations and is a key finding that motivated the development of DASC.

claim: Short-lived clathrin-coated structures are dimmer than mature CCPs detected prior to internalization.
source: Using this imaging approach, we and others have observed that a large fraction of detected clathrin-coated structures (CSs) are shorter-lived (i.e. lifetimes < 20 seconds) than thought to be required for loading and internalizing cargo, and dimmer (i.e. exhibit lower intensities) than mature CCPs detected prior to internalization (Taylor et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations and observational data.

claim: The range of lifetimes and intensities of ACs overlaps substantially with the range of lifetimes and intensities of CCPs.
source: However, the range of lifetimes and intensities of ACs overlaps substantially with the range of lifetimes and intensities of CCPs (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1A,B and is a key challenge addressed by DASC.

claim: The current inability to unambiguously resolve ACs and CCPs limits analyses of the mechanisms governing CCP dynamics and their progression during CME.
source: The current inability to unambiguously resolve ACs and CCPs limits analyses of the mechanisms governing CCP dynamics and their progression during CME.
evidence: This is a statement of the problem that DASC aims to solve.

claim: The distribution of d1 values for wild-type cells is bimodal, allowing the distinction of ACs and CCPs.
source: Indeed, for a population of N > 200,000 CSs tracked in HPV-RPE cells, the distribution of d1 values is bimodal (Figure 1D), allowing the distinction of ACs and CCPs.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1D and is a key result of the DASC method.

claim: The distribution of d2 values is bimodal and can strengthen the distinction between ACs and CCPs.
source: The distribution of this feature is also bimodal (Figure 1E) and thus can strengthen the distinction between ACs and CCPs.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E and supports the DASC classification approach.

claim: The distribution of d3 over N series displays two tight populations with the d3 values of OTs easily separable from the d3 values of ACs and CCPs.
source: The distribution of d3 over N series displays two tight populations with the d3 values of OTs easily separable from the d3 values of ACs and CCPs (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1F and shows that DASC can identify outlier traces.

claim: DASC uses k-medoids clustering to classify ACs, CCPs, and OTs using three summary statistics (d1, d2, d3).
source: Using the three summary statistics (d1,d2,d3) we project all CS traces into a feature space (Figure 2A) and classify ACs (red), CCPs (blue), and OTs (pink) using k-medoids clustering (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the computational method used in DASC, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The lifetimes of ACs were predominantly short (<20 s) and exhibited an exponential distribution characteristic of coats that are exposed to an unregulated disassembly process.
source: The lifetimes of ACs (Figure 2B, red) were predominantly short (<20 s) and exhibited an exponential distribution characteristic of coats that are exposed to an unregulated disassembly process.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and represents a key characteristic of ACs identified by DASC.

claim: CCP lifetimes exhibited a unimodal distribution with a highest probability lifetime of ~26 s.
source: In contrast, CCP lifetimes (Figure 2B, blue) exhibited a unimodal distribution with a highest probability lifetime of ~26 s.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and characterizes CCPs identified by DASC.

claim: The CCP lifetime distribution is best represented by a Rayleigh distribution that reflects the kinetics of a three- to four-step maturation process.
source: In previous work, we had shown that this distribution is best represented by a Rayleigh distribution that reflects the kinetics of a three- to four-step maturation process (Aguet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The intensity distribution of CCPs exhibits a sharp threshold in the minimum intensity, as would be expected given the minimum number of clathrin triskelia required to form a complete clathrin basket.
source: Interestingly, although partially overlapping with ACs, the intensity distribution of CCPs (Figure 2C) exhibits a sharp threshold in the minimum intensity, as would be expected given the minimum number of clathrin triskelia required to form a complete clathrin basket (Grassart et al., 2014; Ehrlich et al., 2004).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C and is supported by citations regarding clathrin basket structure.

claim: CCP intensities rise to a clear maximum as they assemble a complete clathrin coat, followed by a falling limb associated with CCV internalization and/or uncoating.
source: CCP intensities rise to a clear maximum as they assemble a complete clathrin coat (Figure 2Dii), followed by a falling limb, which is associated with CCV internalization and/or uncoating.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2Dii and describes the characteristic intensity profile of CCPs.

claim: AC intensities are lower and more random than CCP intensities, suggesting that these coats undergo continuous exchange of clathrin subunits without significant net assembly.
source: In contrast, AC intensities are lower and more random (Figure 2Diii), suggesting that these coats, trapped in the early growth phase, undergo continuous exchange of clathrin subunits without significant net assembly.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2Diii and represents an interpretation of the AC intensity profiles.

claim: DASC is statistically robust and not overly sensitive to movie-to-movie variations in data collected on the same day.
source: These test results confirmed that no significant difference exists between movies from the same condition. Thus, DASC is statistically robust and not overly sensitive to movie-to-movie variations in data collected on the same day.
evidence: This is supported by the permutation test results shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: DASC is a robust tool to discriminate between two completely distinct clathrin coat assembly and disassembly processes that are associated with abortive coats and bona fide CCPs.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that DASC is a robust tool to discriminate between two completely distinct clathrin coat assembly and disassembly processes that, by inference, are associated with abortive coats and bona fide CCPs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the validation experiments presented.

claim: For all cell lines tested except A549, a clear 'elbow' appears at k=3 in the k-medoids clustering analysis, indicating the optimal cluster/population number is consistently 3.
source: We observed that for all cell lines tested, except for A549, a clear "elbow" appears at k=3 (see Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating the optimal cluster/population number is consistently 3 (Kodinariya and Makwana, 2013).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and validates the choice of k=3 clusters across multiple cell lines.

claim: DASC is reliably transferable to multiple cell lines exhibiting dynamic, diffraction-limited CSs.
source: Nonetheless, from this we conclude that DASC is reliably transferable to multiple cell lines exhibiting dynamic, diffraction-limited CSs.
evidence: This conclusion is based on testing DASC in multiple cell lines as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: AP2 complexes recruit clathrin to the plasma membrane and undergo a series of allosterically-regulated conformational changes needed to stabilize nascent CCPs.
source: AP2 complexes recruit clathrin to the plasma membrane and undergo a series of allosterically-regulated conformational changes needed to stabilize nascent CCPs (Kadlecova et al., 2017; Jackson et al., 2010; Kelly et al., 2008; Collins et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge about AP2 function.

claim: αAP2-PIP2 interactions are critical mediators of AP2 activity.
source: Previous studies based on siRNA-mediated knockdown (KD) of the α subunit of AP2 and reconstitution with either WT, designated αAP2(WT), or a mutant defective in PIP2 binding, designated αAP2(PIP2-), in hTERT-RPE cells have established that αAP2-PIP2 interactions are critical mediators of AP2 activity (Kadlecova et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kadlecova et al., 2017.

claim: DASC analysis revealed an increase in CS initiation rate in αAP2(PIP2-) cells compared to αAP2(WT) cells.
source: We also observed an increase in CS initiation rate (CS init.) (Figure 3Ci), measured by total trackable CSs detected per minute per cell surface area (see Material and methods for detail definition).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3Ci and represents a DASC-derived measurement.

claim: DASC analysis revealed a pronounced decrease in the efficiency of CCP stabilization (measured as CCP%) in αAP2(PIP2-) cells compared to αAP2(WT) cells.
source: We detected a pronounced decrease in the efficiency of CCP stabilization, measured as CCP% (Figure 3Cii), which was calculated as the fraction of CCPs in all the valid traces (see Material and methods).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3Cii and demonstrates DASC's ability to detect stabilization defects.

claim: The lifetime distributions of CCPs shifted to shorter lifetimes in αAP2(PIP2-) cells compared to αAP2(WT) cells.
source: The lifetime distributions of CCPs also shifted to shorter lifetimes (Figure 3Ciii, left panel), resulting in decreased median lifetimes (Table 1) in αAP2(PIP2-) cells compared to αAP2(WT) cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3Ciii and Table 1.

claim: The initial rates of recruitment to CSs of both clathrin and AP2 were much greater for CCPs than ACs.
source: Moreover, as previously shown for statistically-defined abortive vs. productive pits (Loerke et al., 2011), the initial rates of recruitment to CSs of both clathrin and AP2, determined by the derivative of intensity, were much greater for CCPs than ACs (Figure 3Ei–ii).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3Ei-ii and is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DASC-defined CCPs in the 20s cohort reached maxima invagination depth Δzmax/h>0.3, which corresponds to an invagination depth of >35nm.
source: DASC-defined CCPs in the 20s cohort reached maxima Δzmax/h=max[Δz(t)]/h>0.3 (Figure 3F), which corresponds to an invagination depth of >35nm (h=115nm is the characteristic depth of our TIRF illumination field, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F and demonstrates that DASC-identified CCPs acquire curvature.

claim: DASC-defined ACs in the 20 s cohort fail to gain significant curvature.
source: In contrast, DASC-defined ACs in the 20 s cohort fail to gain significant curvature.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: DASC-resolved ACs and CCPs are structurally and functionally distinct.
source: Together, these data establish that DASC-resolved ACs and CCPs are, indeed, structurally and functionally distinct.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the curvature measurements and other validation experiments.

claim: KD of CALM dramatically decreased initiation, stabilization and TfReff.
source: KD of CALM dramatically decreased initiation (Figure 4B), stabilization (Figure 4C) and TfReff (Figure 4F), and also significantly altered the lifetime distribution of CCPs (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4B, C, E, and F.

claim: KD of epsin1 selectively perturbed CCP stabilization without affecting initiation, CCP lifetime or TfReff.
source: Conversely, KD of epsin1 selectively perturbed CCP stabilization without affecting initiation, CCP lifetime or TfReff (Figure 4B–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4B-F and demonstrates DASC's ability to detect stage-specific effects.

claim: Initiation and stabilization were significantly decreased upon KD of Eps15, while CCP lifetime was not significantly affected.
source: Initiation and stabilization were significantly decreased upon KD of Eps15, while CCP lifetime was not significantly affected; on the other hand, TfReff was slightly increased (Figure 4F), suggesting a compensatory effect.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4B-F.

claim: FCHO1/2, ITSN1/2, NECAP1 and Eps15/15R selectively altered CCP initiation and/or stabilization without affecting CCP maturation rates.
source: From this we observe that FCHO1/2, ITSN1/2, NECAP1 and Eps15/15R (Ma et al., 2016) selectively altered CCP initiation and/or stabilization without affecting CCP maturation rates, and have only relatively mild effects on the efficiency of TfR uptake (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: DASC is a statistically reliable method to detect and distinguish phenotypes caused by KD of individual EAPs.
source: In sum, DASC is a statistically reliable method to detect and distinguish phenotypes caused by KD of individual EAPs, thus enabling their effects on specific stage(s) of CCP dynamics to be mechanistically dissected.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the EAP knockdown experiments.

claim: EAPs that affected CCP median lifetime (CALM, SNX9, NECAP1 and ITSN2) also exhibited the strongest effects on cargo uptake.
source: However, those that did (i.e. CALM, SNX9, NECAP1 and ITSN2) also exhibited the strongest effects on cargo uptake.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: DASC provides increased sensitivity and greater phenotypic resolution over bulk biochemical measurements of cargo uptake.
source: These comparisons highlight the value of DASC for increased sensitivity and greater phenotypic resolution over bulk biochemical measurements of cargo uptake, which can often obscure effects of EAP KD due to the resilience of CME.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the comparison of DASC measurements with transferrin uptake assays.

claim: DASC accurately separates dynamically, structurally and functionally distinct CS subpopulations without imposing any prior assumptions or the need for additional markers.
source: The associated software pipeline, DASC, reliably separates dynamically, structurally and functionally distinct CS subpopulations without imposing any prior assumptions or the need for additional markers.
evidence: This is a summary statement about DASC's capabilities based on the validation experiments.

claim: ACs have much lower average intensities than CCPs.
source: Characterization of the DASC-resolved AC and CCP subpopulations shows that ACs: i) have much lower average intensities than CCPs
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs.

claim: ACs have much shorter average lifetimes than CCPs.
source: ii) have much shorter average lifetimes than CCPs
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs.

claim: ACs exhibit unregulated exponentially decaying lifetime distributions, as compared to the Rayleigh distributed CCP lifetimes.
source: iii) exhibit unregulated exponentially decaying lifetime distributions, as compared to the Rayleigh distributed CCP lifetimes
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs.

claim: ACs contain fewer AP2 complexes than CCPs.
source: iv) contain fewer AP2 complexes than CCPs
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs based on dual-channel imaging.

claim: ACs recruit both clathrin and AP2 at a much slower rate than CCPs.
source: v) recruit both clathrin and AP2 at a much slower rate than CCPs
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs based on dual-channel imaging.

claim: ACs acquire less curvature than CCPs.
source: vi) acquire less curvature than CCPs
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of DASC-resolved ACs based on EPI-TIRF measurements.

claim: DASC is a powerful new tool for stratifying individual CSs into ACs and CCPs and is uniquely applicable to single channel imaging.
source: DASC is thus a powerful new tool for stratifying individual CSs into these groups and is uniquely applicable to single channel imaging.
evidence: This is a summary statement about DASC's advantages.

claim: DASC imposes certain requirements on the processed movies, including sampling near the frequency of clathrin exchange with the assembling coat.
source: To satisfy this condition, DASC imposes certain requirements on the processed movies. First, movies need to be sampled near the frequency of clathrin exchange with the assembling coat.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for DASC application.

claim: Several studies have documented a unit turnover at the scale of ~2s for clathrin, based on fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) measurements.
source: Several studies have documented a unit turnover at the scale of ~2s, based on fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) measurements (Avinoam et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2001; Loerke et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: All movies analyzed in this study were acquired at a frame rate of 1 s−1.
source: Accordingly, all our movies were acquired at a frame rate of 1 s−1.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Movies must provide sufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for the detection of the dim, AC-related structures.
source: In addition, the movies must provide sufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for the detection of the dim, AC-related structures.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for DASC analysis.

claim: Cells expressing endogenous levels of fluorescent clathrin generate too dim a signal for the analysis of early coat assembly.
source: As discussed before (Aguet et al., 2013), even with the most efficient camera equipment for image capture, cells expressing endogenous levels of fluorescent clathrin generate too dim a signal for the analysis of early coat assembly (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Movies must be long enough to capture the vast majority of long-lived CSs without truncation artifacts.
source: Finally, movies must be long enough to capture the vast majority of long-lived CSs without truncation artifacts. In our case, we filmed cells for 7.5 minutes.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for DASC analysis.

claim: While a burst of Dyn2-eGFP recruitment often occurs at later stages of CCP maturation, the timing and intensity of these bursts vary considerably.
source: For example, while a burst of Dyn2-eGFP recruitment often occurs at later stages of CCP maturation, accompanying membrane fission, the timing and intensity of these bursts vary considerably (Taylor et al., 2011; Cocucci et al., 2014); and in some cases are undetectable (Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations and discusses limitations of using dynamin as a marker.

claim: CCPs lacking detectable Dyn2 were, on average, shorter-lived than those bearing Dyn2, but the lifetime distributions of these two populations significantly overlap.
source: Although CCPs lacking detectable Dyn2 were indeed, on average, shorter-lived than those bearing Dyn2, the lifetime distributions of these two populations significantly overlap (Aguet et al., 2013; Ehrlich et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Dyn2 has been shown to be recruited at earlier stages in parallel to CCP growth.
source: Moreover, Dyn2 has been shown to be recruited at earlier stages in parallel to CCP growth (Aguet et al., 2013; Ehrlich et al., 2004; Taylor et al., 2012; Cocucci et al., 2014), and has been suggested to function in regulating the turnover of abortive pits (Loerke et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The recruitment of Dyn2 does not unambiguously distinguish ACs from CCPs.
source: Thus, the recruitment of Dyn2 does not unambiguously distinguish ACs from CCPs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cited evidence about Dyn2 recruitment.

claim: The only unambiguous marker of a productive fission event is the internalization of pH sensitive-cargo.
source: Currently, the only unambiguous marker of a productive fission event is the internalization of pH sensitive-cargo (Taylor et al., 2011), with the obvious drawback of requiring a complex perfusion apparatus and 3-color imaging.
evidence: This is supported by citation and discusses the gold standard for identifying productive CCPs.

claim: CCPs with higher concentrations of TfR tend to have longer lifetimes than those bearing fewer TfR, although there is significant overlap.
source: Others have suggested that cargo recruitment is a critical determinant of CCP maturation (Loerke et al., 2009; Ehrlich et al., 2004), and indeed CCPs with higher concentrations of TfR tend to have longer lifetimes than those bearing fewer TfR (Liu et al., 2010), although again there is significant overlap.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: AP2-cargo interactions are essential for activation of AP2 complexes and for CCP initiation and stabilization.
source: However, because AP2-cargo interactions are essential for activation of AP2 complexes (Jackson et al., 2010) and for CCP initiation and stabilization (Kadlecova et al., 2017), cargo loading is also not a definitive molecular marker for ACs vs CCPs.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: TfR intensity has been shown to correlate precisely with clathrin intensity in both small and large CCPs.
source: Indeed, TfR intensity has been shown to correlate precisely with clathrin intensity in both small and large CCPs (Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The rate and extent of AP2 recruitment to nascent CCPs is a distinguishing feature of ACs and CCPs.
source: Interestingly, we have shown that the rate and extent of AP2 recruitment to nascent CCPs, which might be a surrogate for cargo recruitment, is a distinguishing feature of ACs and CCPs.
evidence: This is based on the dual-channel imaging results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Combinations of interdependent molecules rather than a single molecular event will be needed to drive and define productive endocytic events.
source: We speculate that combinations of interdependent molecules rather than a single molecular event will be needed to drive and therefore define productive endocytic events.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the findings.

claim: The CCPs identified by DASC likely encompass a fraction of late abortive CCPs whose numbers will increase when the endocytic checkpoint is triggered.
source: We expect that the CCPs identified by DASC also encompass a fraction of late abortive CCPs whose numbers will increase when the endocytic checkpoint is triggered.
evidence: This is stated as an expectation based on previous work.

claim: Efficient CCP maturation is likely driven by a complex mixture of conditionally coupled EAPs.
source: Given the robustness of CME and the functional redundancy of EAPs, we underline again that efficient CCP maturation is likely driven by a complex mixture of conditionally coupled EAPs and that the compositional differences between productive and late abortive CCPs thus will be quantitative (i.e. determined by conditional probability distributions) rather than qualitative (i.e. all or none).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: DASC enables sensitive, phenotypic assignment of individual EAPs to discrete stages of CME.
source: Thus, DASC enables sensitive, phenotypic assignment of individual EAPs to discrete stages of CME.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the EAP knockdown experiments.

claim: The poor/lack of correlation between CCP rate and transferrin uptake suggests the existence of compensatory mechanisms and/or molecular redundancy.
source: The poor/lack of correlation between CCP rate and transferrin uptake suggests the existence of compensatory mechanisms (Aguet et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2017) and/or molecular redundancy (Kirchhausen et al., 2014) that could account for restoring or maintaining efficient cargo uptake.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Multiple genome-wide screens based on ligand internalization assays failed to detect EAPs, demonstrating the resilient aspects of CME.
source: These resilient aspects of CME against the effects of KD of individual components of the endocytic machinery are also evident in the inability of multiple genome-wide screens based on ligand internalization assays to detect EAPs (Kozik et al., 2013; Bassik et al., 2013; Gulbranson et al., 2019; Collinet et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: DASC will be a critical tool for future studies aimed at identifying possible compensatory mechanisms able to restore transferrin receptor internalization.
source: Thus, DASC will be a critical tool for future studies aimed at identifying possible compensatory mechanisms able to restore transferrin receptor internalization.
evidence: This is stated as a future application of DASC.

claim: CCP maturation is controlled by an endocytic checkpoint.
source: In particular, we and others (Aguet et al., 2013; Loerke et al., 2009; Ehrlich et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2019) have proposed that CCP maturation is controlled by an endocytic checkpoint.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The molecular nature of the endocytic checkpoint has remained elusive, in part because of the complexities in characterizing multi-component molecular machinery.
source: While the existence of such a checkpoint was inferred from statistical analysis of CS lifetimes and associated considerations of the maturation kinetics (Aguet et al., 2013; Loerke et al., 2009), the molecular nature of this checkpoint has remained elusive, in part because of the complexities in characterizing multi-component molecular machinery.
evidence: This is supported by citations and states a current limitation in the field.

claim: DASC's single-marker classification of ACs and CCPs opens an opportunity to identify the molecular conditions of the endocytic checkpoint through multichannel imaging of EAPs.
source: DASC's single-marker classification of ACs and CCPs opens an opportunity to identify the molecular conditions of such a checkpoint through multichannel imaging of EAPs, especially of early EAPs.
evidence: This is stated as a future application of DASC.

claim: The effects on TfR uptake observed in this study for CALM and SNX9 differ from some previous reports showing only minor or no effects.
source: We report a strong effect on the efficiency of TfR uptake in cells depleted of CALM and SNX9, whereas others have reported only minor or no effects (Xiao et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2004; Posor et al., 2013; Bendris et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Differences in effects on TfR uptake may reflect cell type specific expression levels and/or activities of functionally redundant isoforms.
source: These differences may reflect cell type specific expression levels and/or activities of functionally redundant isoforms such as AP180 or SNX18 in the case of CALM and SNX9, respectively (Posor et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation supported by citation.

claim: The effects on TfR uptake correlate most strongly with the effects on CCP maturation resulting from depletion of CALM, SNX9 and other EAPs.
source: Interestingly, the effects we observe on TfR uptake correlate most strongly with the effects on CCP maturation resulting from depletion of CALM, SNX9 and, to a lesser extent, other EAPs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: DASC is more sensitive than TfR uptake assays and uncorrelated to them.
source: Nonetheless, being uncorrelated to but more sensitive than TfR uptake assays, DASC perhaps suggests a limitation of using deterministic biochemical approaches to study mesoscopic systems that are molecularly dense and complex, like CME.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: DASC classifies the previously unresolvable ACs and CCPs using data derived from single channel live cell TIRF imaging.
source: In summary, DASC classifies the previously unresolvable ACs and CCPs using data derived from single channel live cell TIRF imaging, thus providing an accurate measure of progression of CME through its early stages.
evidence: This is a summary statement of DASC's capabilities.

claim: DASC is essential to functionally and comprehensively characterize the roles of the complete set of >70 EAPs in CME dynamics.
source: Going forward, DASC will be essential to functionally and comprehensively characterize the roles of the complete set of >70 EAPs in CME dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a future application of DASC.

claim: ARPE19/HPV16 cells were infected with lentivirus encoding eGFP-tagged clathrin light chain a (eGFP-CLCa) and selected for stable expression at ~5-fold over endogenous levels.
source: To ensure high sensitivity detection of all CCP initiation events, ARPE19/HPV16 (hereafter called HPV-RPE) cells were infected with lentivirus encoding an eGFP-tagged clathrin light chain a (eGFP-CLCa) and then selected for those that stably expressed eGFP-CLCa at ~ 5-fold over endogenous levels.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Overexpression of eGFP-CLCa ensures near stoichiometric incorporation of fluorescently-labeled CLC into clathrin triskelia by displacing both endogenous CLCa and CLCb.
source: Overexpression of eGFP-CLCa ensures near stoichiometric incorporation of fluorescently-labeled CLC into clathrin triskelia by displacing both endogenous CLCa and CLCb.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Under conditions of ~5-fold overexpression of eGFP-CLCa, CME is unperturbed and eGFP-CLCa serves as a robust fiduciary marker for coated pit dynamics at the plasma membrane.
source: Control experiments by numerous labs have established that under these conditions CME is unperturbed and that eGFP-CLCa serves as a robust fiduciary marker for coated pit dynamics at the plasma membrane (Aguet et al., 2013; Taylor et al., 2011; Loerke et al., 2009; Ehrlich et al., 2004; Miller et al., 2015; Gaidarov et al., 1999; Cocucci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: For all conditions, ≥ 19 independent movies were collected and the eGFP intensities of >200,000 clathrin structures per condition were tracked over time.
source: For all conditions, ≥ 19 independent movies were collected and the eGFP intensities of >200,000 clathrin structures per condition were tracked over time using TIRFM and established automated image analysis pipelines (Aguet et al., 2013; Jaqaman et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Bona fide CCPs tend to have lifetimes > 20 s and approach an intensity level corresponding to a fully assembled coat (between 36 and > 60 triskelia).
source: Bona fide CCPs tend to have lifetimes > 20 s and approach an intensity level corresponding to a fully assembled coat (between 36 and > 60 triskelia) (Ehrlich et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: ACs tend to exhibit lower intensity levels and disassemble at any time.
source: In contrast, ACs tend to exhibit lower intensity levels and disassemble at any time.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of ACs.

claim: The intensities of individual CSs are highly fluctuating due to low signal:noise, rapid turnover of individual triskelia, stochastic bleaching of fluorophores, camera noise and membrane fluctuations.
source: Significantly compounding the ability to distinguish CCPs from ACs is the fact that the intensities of individual CSs are highly fluctuating (see for example, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B). These fluctuations are inevitable and reflect a combination of low signal:noise (especially during early stages of CCP growth and maturation), rapid turnover of individual triskelia, which occurs on the time scale of ~2 s (Kirchhausen et al., 2014; Avinoam et al., 2015), stochastic bleaching of fluorophores, camera noise and membrane fluctuations within the TIRF field.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B, with citations supporting the turnover rate.

claim: The computation of entropy production (EP) quantifies the dissipation rate of thermal energy when a system is driven far away from equilibrium.
source: Inspired by the computation of entropy production (EP) (Seifert, 2005), we designed a new metric derived from the fluctuations of clathrin intensity traces that can clearly separate ACs from CCPs. Conventionally, EP quantifies the dissipation rate of thermal energy when a system of interest is driven far away from equilibrium, as is the case during the formation of a macro-molecular assembly such as a CCP.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seifert, 2005.

claim: D(i,t)<0 is indicative of early stages of clathrin recruitment when disassembly risk is suppressed.
source: In summary, D(i,t)<0 is indicative of early stages of clathrin recruitment when disassembly risk is suppressed
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the D function.

claim: For maturing CCPs, D values distribute around zero, whereas for ACs D values distribute in the negative range.
source: Thus, for maturing CCPs D values distribute around zero, whereas for ACs D values distribute in the negative range.
evidence: This is stated as a key distinguishing feature between ACs and CCPs.
